chunks: Al-Sakuni narrated from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام:
He was asked about a man who bequeaths a share of his wealth, so he said:
The share is one out of eight, based on the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

"Indeed, the charities are only for the poor, the needy, those employed over them, those whose hearts are to be reconciled, for freeing slaves, for those in debt, in the way of Allah, and the stranded traveler."

key_terms.ابْنِ السَّبِيلِ: The stranded traveler cut off from resources.
key_terms.الصَّدَقَاتُ: Charitable funds distributed to designated recipients.
key_terms.ثَمَانِيَةٍ: Eight parts or categories, used here as the legal basis for defining the share.
key_terms.سَهْمٍ: A share or allotted portion of property.
key_terms.يُوصِي: He makes a bequest through a will.

ai.seo_question: If someone bequeaths a "share" of his wealth, how much is meant in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on a bequest described simply as a "share" of one’s wealth. Imam Abu Abdullah عليه السلام explains that such a share means one of eight parts, deriving the meaning from the eight categories named in the Qur'anic verse on ṣadaqāt.
